title: And Then There Were None
author: Agatha Christie
summary: A brilliant pick if you enjoy detective novels. It's a true mystery — you never know what's coming next, and it keeps you hooked from start to finish. You just don't want to put it down.

title: Rich Dad Poor Dad
author: Robert Kiyosaki
summary: The core idea is distinguishing assets from liabilities: buy things that put money in your pocket and avoid things that take money out. It also covers understanding taxes, learning what you are good at, and delegating rather than doing everything yourself.

title: The Richest Man in Babylon
author: George S. Clason
summary: Teaches practical principles for managing money: pay yourself first, invest wisely, and work hard and consistently to build wealth over time.

title: Who Not How
author: Dan Sullivan & Benjamin Hardy
summary: Focuses on finding the right people to work with rather than trying to do everything yourself. It teaches how to build a strong team, identify what the team is missing, and lead effectively by delegating to the right who instead of figuring out the how alone.

title: Eat That Frog
author: Brian Tracy
summary: A productivity book offering 21 ways to stop procrastinating and get the most important things done first.

title: Atomic Habits
author: James Clear
summary: Explains how small, consistent habits compound into major change over time, and lays out a clear framework for building good habits and breaking bad ones.

title: Mehrobdan Chayon
author: Abdulla Qodiriy
summary: An engaging historical novel that vividly portrays life in that era.

author: George Orwell
summary: A well-written book. Some parts feel boring, but it gets exciting quickly. It clearly shows how a government can control people and keep them obedient and loyal to the state.

title: Animal Farm
author: George Orwell
summary: The animals drive out their owner to build a life of their own, but the cleverest among them take power and turn on the rest — deceiving the simpler animals, convincing them every decision is right, and pushing out honest voices through slander or force. Close in spirit to 1984 in how it exposes the machinery of tyranny, and clearly drawn from a real revolution.

title: Ikigai
author: Héctor García & Francesc Miralles
summary: Explores why people in Japan, especially in Okinawa, often live long and happy lives. The key idea is ikigai: your reason to get up every morning. It’s what keeps many Japanese people working and staying active even in their 90s. The book shows how finding your ikigai, along with healthy daily habits, can help anyone live longer and happier.

title: Surely You're Joking, Mr. Feynman!
author: Richard P. Feynman
summary: The autobiography of Richard Feynman, the physicist who won the Nobel Prize for his work on quantum electrodynamics. Told as a series of funny stories, it shows his endless curiosity. He made his own math symbols so he could understand things better, found new ways to solve problems, and worked on the atomic bomb at Los Alamos. He didn't stop at physics. He studied biology and art too, and got good enough at them to be skilled in both. He also taught himself safe-cracking and played the drums.
